title.en: Biography of Tian Dan, King of Qi
title.raw: 《田儋列傳》 Biography of Tian Dan, King of Qi

sentences.zh: 田儋者，狄人也，故齊王田氏族也。

translations.literal: Tian Dan was a man of Di. He was of the clan of the former kings of Qi, the Tian family.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dan was a native of Di and a descendant of the Tian clan, the former royal house of Qi.

sentences.zh: 儋從弟田榮，榮弟田橫，皆豪，宗彊，能得人。

translations.literal: Dan's cousin Tian Rong, and Rong's younger brother Tian Heng, were all bold and formidable. Their clan was powerful and they could win men over.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Tian Rong and Rong's younger brother Tian Heng were both bold and formidable men. Their clan wielded great power and could rally followers to their cause.

sentences.zh: 陳涉之初起王楚也，使周市略定魏地，北至狄，狄城守。

translations.literal: When Chen She first rose and declared himself king of Chu, he sent Zhou Shi to raid and pacify the lands of Wei, reaching north to Di, where Di defended its city.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen She first rose in revolt and proclaimed himself King of Chu, he dispatched Zhou Shi to subdue the territory of Wei. Zhou Shi advanced north as far as Di, but the city held fast against him.

sentences.zh: 田儋詳為縛其奴，從少年之廷，欲謁殺奴。

translations.literal: Tian Dan pretended to bind his slave and followed some youths to the county court, intending to meet with the magistrate and kill the slave.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dan feigned having a slave bound and, accompanied by a group of young men, proceeded to the county court under the pretext of petitioning for the slave's execution.

sentences.zh: 見狄令，因擊殺令，而召豪吏子弟曰：「諸侯皆反秦自立，齊，古之建國，儋，田氏，當王。」

translations.literal: When he saw the magistrate of Di, he struck and killed him, then summoned the sons of the bold officials and said, "All the lords have rebelled against Qin and established themselves. Qi is an ancient state; I, Dan of the Tian clan, ought to be king."
translations.idiomatic: When he gained audience with the magistrate of Di, he struck the man dead. He then summoned the sons of the local notables and declared, "All the lords have risen against Qin and proclaimed their own kingdoms. Qi is an ancient state, and I, Tian Dan of the Tian clan, ought to be its king."

sentences.zh: 遂自立為齊王，發兵以擊周市。

translations.literal: He then established himself as King of Qi and sent troops to attack Zhou Shi.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon declared himself King of Qi and mustered troops to strike against Zhou Shi.

sentences.zh: 周市軍還去，田儋因率兵東略定齊地。

translations.literal: Zhou Shi's army retreated, and Tian Dan then led troops east to raid and pacify the lands of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shi's forces withdrew, and Tian Dan led his army eastward to bring the lands of Qi under his control.

sentences.zh: 秦將章邯圍魏王咎於臨濟，急。

translations.literal: The Qin general Zhang Han besieged King Jiu of Wei at Linji, and the situation was urgent.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin general Zhang Han laid siege to King Jiu of Wei at Linji, and the situation grew desperate.

sentences.zh: 魏王請救於齊，齊王田儋將兵救魏。

translations.literal: The King of Wei requested aid from Qi, and King Tian Dan of Qi led troops to save Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wei appealed to Qi for help, and King Tian Dan of Qi marched his forces to Wei's relief.

sentences.zh: 章邯夜銜枚擊，大破齊、魏軍，殺田儋於臨濟下。

translations.literal: Zhang Han attacked at night with wooden gags in their mouths, greatly defeating the Qi and Wei armies, killing Tian Dan below Linji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han launched a surprise night attack, his soldiers biting down on wooden gags to maintain silence, and routed the combined Qi and Wei forces, slaying Tian Dan beneath the walls of Linji.

sentences.zh: 儋弟田榮收儋餘兵東走東阿。

translations.literal: Dan's younger brother Tian Rong gathered Dan's remaining troops and fled east to Dong'e.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dan's kinsman Tian Rong rallied the remnants of Dan's army and retreated east to Dong'e.

sentences.zh: 齊人聞王田儋死，乃立故齊王建之弟田假為齊王、田角為相、田間為將，以距諸侯。

translations.literal: When the people of Qi heard that King Tian Dan had died, they installed Tian Jia, younger brother of the former Qi king Jian, as king of Qi, made Tian Jiao chancellor, and made Tian Jian general, in order to resist the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Qi heard that King Tian Dan was dead, they set up Tian Jia, younger brother of the former Qi king Jian, as king of Qi; appointed Tian Jiao chancellor; and made Tian Jian general, so as to resist the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 田榮之走東阿，章邯追圍之。

translations.literal: When Tian Rong fled to Dong'e, Zhang Han pursued and besieged him.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Rong fell back to Dong'e, Zhang Han gave chase and laid siege to the city.

sentences.zh: 項梁聞田榮之急，乃引兵擊破章邯軍東阿下。

translations.literal: Xiang Liang heard of Tian Rong's urgency and led troops to attack and break Zhang Han's army below Dong'e.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Liang, hearing of Tian Rong's dire straits, brought his forces to bear and shattered Zhang Han's army beneath the walls of Dong'e.

sentences.zh: 章邯走而西，項梁因追之。

translations.literal: Zhang Han fled west, and Xiang Liang then pursued him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han fled westward, and Xiang Liang gave pursuit.

sentences.zh: 而田榮怒齊之立假，乃引兵歸，擊逐齊王假。

translations.literal: But Tian Rong was angry that Qi had set up Tian Jia as king, so he led troops back and attacked, driving out King Tian Jia of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: But Tian Rong, furious that Qi had installed Tian Jia as king, led his troops home and drove King Jia from the throne.

sentences.zh: 假亡走楚。

translations.literal: Tian Jia fled to Chu.
translations.idiomatic: King Jia fled to Chu.

sentences.zh: 齊相角亡走趙；

translations.literal: Qi Chancellor Jiao fled to Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor of Qi, Tian Jiao, fled to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 角弟田閒前求救趙，因留不敢歸。

translations.literal: Jiao's younger brother Tian Jian had previously sought aid from Zhao and stayed there, not daring to return.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao's younger brother Tian Jian had earlier gone to Zhao to seek aid and remained there, not daring to return.

sentences.zh: 田榮乃立田儋子市為齊王。

translations.literal: Tian Rong then established Tian Dan's son Shi as King of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Rong then installed Tian Dan's son Shi as King of Qi.

sentences.zh: 榮相之，田橫為將，平齊地。

translations.literal: Rong served as his chancellor, and Tian Heng as general, pacifying the lands of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Rong served as chancellor and Tian Heng as general, and together they pacified the lands of Qi.

sentences.zh: 項梁既追章邯，章邯兵益盛，項梁使使告趙、齊，發兵共擊章邯。

translations.literal: After Xiang Liang pursued Zhang Han, Zhang Han's troops became increasingly strong. Xiang Liang sent envoys to tell Zhao and Qi to send troops together to attack Zhang Han.
translations.idiomatic: As Xiang Liang continued to pursue Zhang Han, Zhang Han's forces grew ever stronger. Xiang Liang sent envoys to Zhao and Qi, urging them to commit troops for a joint attack on Zhang Han.

sentences.zh: 田榮曰：「使楚殺田假，趙殺田角、田閒，閒肯出兵。」

translations.literal: Tian Rong said, "Have Chu kill Tian Jia, and have Zhao kill Tian Jiao and Tian Jian—only then will I send troops."
translations.idiomatic: Tian Rong replied, "Have Chu execute Tian Jia, and have Zhao execute Tian Jiao and Tian Jian—only then will I send troops."

sentences.zh: 楚懷王曰：「田假與國之王，窮而歸我，殺之不義。」

translations.literal: King Huai of Chu said, "Tian Jia was king of an allied state. In distress he came to me; to kill him would be unrighteous."
translations.idiomatic: King Huai of Chu said, "Tian Jia was king of an allied state. He came to me in his hour of need—to kill him would be unjust."

sentences.zh: 趙亦不殺田角、田閒以市於齊。

translations.literal: Zhao also did not kill Tian Jiao and Tian Jian in order to trade with Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao likewise refused to execute Tian Jiao and Tian Jian as a concession to Qi.

sentences.zh: 齊曰：「蝮螫手則斬手，螫足則斬足。

translations.literal: Qi said, "When a viper stings the hand, cut off the hand; when it stings the foot, cut off the foot.
translations.idiomatic: Qi replied, "When a viper stings the hand, you cut off the hand; when it stings the foot, you cut off the foot.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: What?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 為害於身也。

translations.literal: Because it harms the body.
translations.idiomatic: Because the venom would kill the whole body.

sentences.zh: 今田假、田角、田閒於楚、趙，非直手足戚也，何故不殺？

translations.literal: Now Tian Jia, Tian Jiao, and Tian Jian are in Chu and Zhao. They are no mere sting to hand or foot—why do you not kill them?
translations.idiomatic: Now Tian Jia, Tian Jiao, and Tian Jian are sheltered in Chu and Zhao. They are no mere sting to hand or foot—why will you not kill them?

sentences.zh: 且秦復得志於天下，則齮龁用事者墳墓矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover, if Qin again achieves its ambition in the empire, those who took power against it will be ground to dust in their graves."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if Qin prevails once more over the world, those who held power against it will be gnawed to dust in their graves."

sentences.zh: 楚、趙不聽，齊亦怒，終不肯出兵。

translations.literal: Chu and Zhao did not listen, and Qi was also angry, finally unwilling to send troops.
translations.idiomatic: Chu and Zhao refused to comply, and Qi in turn grew resentful, ultimately refusing to send any troops.

sentences.zh: 章邯果敗殺項梁，破楚兵，楚兵東走，而章邯渡河圍趙於鉅鹿。

translations.literal: Zhang Han indeed defeated and killed Xiang Liang, broke the Chu troops, and the Chu troops fled east. Zhang Han then crossed the river and besieged Zhao at Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Sure enough, Zhang Han defeated and killed Xiang Liang, shattering the Chu forces and sending them fleeing east. Zhang Han then crossed the Yellow River and besieged Zhao at Julu.

sentences.zh: 項羽往救趙，由此怨田榮。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu went to save Zhao, and from this resented Tian Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu marched to Zhao's rescue, and from that time bore a deep grudge against Tian Rong.

sentences.zh: 項羽既存趙，降章邯等，西屠咸陽，滅秦而立侯王也，乃徙齊王田市更王膠東，治即墨。

translations.literal: After Xiang Yu preserved Zhao and Zhang Han and others surrendered, he went west to slaughter Xianyang, extinguished Qin, and established the various lords and kings. He then moved King Tian Shi of Qi to be king of Jiaodong, governing from Jimo.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiang Yu saved Zhao and accepted the surrender of Zhang Han and his forces, he marched west to sack Xianyang, destroyed Qin, and parceled out the realm among the lords. He transferred King Tian Shi of Qi to the Kingdom of Jiaodong, with his seat at Jimo.

sentences.zh: 齊將田都從共救趙，因入關，故立都為齊王，治臨淄。

translations.literal: The Qi general Tian Du followed and helped save Zhao, and then entered the pass. Therefore, he was established as King of Qi, governing from Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi general Tian Du had joined the campaign to rescue Zhao and afterward entered the passes with the allied forces. For this he was made King of Qi, with his seat at Linzi.

sentences.zh: 故齊王建孫田安，項羽方渡河救趙，田安下濟北數城，引兵降項羽，項羽立田安為濟北王，治博陽。

translations.literal: The grandson of the former King Jian of Qi, Tian An, when Xiang Yu was crossing the river to save Zhao, took several cities in Jibei and led troops to surrender to Xiang Yu. Xiang Yu established Tian An as King of Jibei, governing from Boyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tian An, a grandson of the former King Jian of Qi, had seized several cities in Jibei while Xiang Yu was crossing the river to relieve Zhao, and brought his forces over in submission. For this, Xiang Yu made him King of Jibei, with his seat at Boyang.

sentences.zh: 田榮以負項梁不肯出兵助楚、趙攻秦，故不得王；

translations.literal: Tian Rong, because he had failed Xiang Liang and refused to send troops to aid Chu and Zhao in attacking Qin, was not made a king.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Rong, because he had failed Xiang Liang and refused to send troops to aid Chu and Zhao against Qin, was denied a kingdom.

sentences.zh: 趙將陳餘亦失職，不得王：二人俱怨項王。

translations.literal: The Zhao general Chen Yu likewise failed to obtain a kingdom. Both men resented King Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao general Chen Yu had likewise been passed over and denied a kingdom. Both men harbored a deep resentment toward King Xiang.

sentences.zh: 頊王既歸，諸侯各就國，田榮使人將兵助陳餘，令反趙地，而榮亦發兵以距擊田都，田都亡走楚。

translations.literal: After King Xiang returned, the various lords each went to their states. Tian Rong sent men with troops to help Chen Yu, ordering him to rebel in Zhao territory, while Rong also sent troops to resist and attack Tian Du. Tian Du fled to Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Once King Xiang returned west and the lords dispersed to their kingdoms, Tian Rong sent troops to aid Chen Yu, directing him to seize Zhao. At the same time, Rong raised his own forces and attacked Tian Du, who fled to Chu.

sentences.zh: 田榮留齊王市，無令之膠東。

translations.literal: Tian Rong detained King Shi of Qi and did not order him to go to Jiaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Rong kept King Shi in Qi and forbade him from proceeding to Jiaodong.

sentences.zh: 市之左右曰：「項王彊暴，而王當之膠東，不就國，必危。」

translations.literal: Shi's attendants said, "King Xiang is violent and overbearing. Your Majesty is assigned to Jiaodong; if you do not go to your kingdom, you will surely be in peril."
translations.idiomatic: Shi's attendants warned him, "King Xiang is powerful and ruthless. You have been assigned to Jiaodong—if you do not go to your kingdom, you will surely be in danger."

sentences.zh: 市懼，乃亡就國。

translations.literal: Shi was afraid and fled to his state.
translations.idiomatic: Shi grew afraid and slipped away to take up his kingdom.

sentences.zh: 田榮怒，追擊殺齊王市於即墨，還攻殺濟北王安。

translations.literal: Tian Rong was angry, pursued and attacked, killing King Shi of Qi at Jimo. He returned and attacked, killing King An of Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Rong, enraged, gave chase and killed King Shi at Jimo. He then turned back and attacked and killed King An of Jibei.

sentences.zh: 於是田榮乃自立為齊王，盡并三齊之地。

translations.literal: Tian Rong then established himself as King of Qi, completely annexing all the lands of the three Qi regions.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Rong thereupon proclaimed himself King of Qi, bringing all three Qi kingdoms under his rule.

sentences.zh: 項王聞之，大怒，乃北伐齊。

translations.literal: King Xiang heard of it and was greatly angered. He then attacked Qi to the north.
translations.idiomatic: When King Xiang learned of this, he flew into a rage and marched north to punish Qi.

sentences.zh: 齊王田榮兵敗，走平原，平原人殺榮。

translations.literal: King Tian Rong of Qi suffered defeat, fled to Pingyuan, and the people of Pingyuan killed Rong.
translations.idiomatic: King Tian Rong of Qi was defeated in battle and fled to Pingyuan, where the people of that place killed him.

sentences.zh: 項王遂燒夷齊城郭，所過者盡屠之。

translations.literal: King Xiang then burned and razed the cities and walls of Qi, slaughtering all those he passed.
translations.idiomatic: King Xiang then burned and leveled the cities of Qi, putting to the sword everyone in his path.

sentences.zh: 齊人相聚畔之。

translations.literal: The people of Qi gathered together and rebelled against him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Qi banded together and rose against him.

sentences.zh: 榮弟橫，收齊散兵，得數萬人，反擊項羽於城陽。

translations.literal: Rong's younger brother Heng gathered Qi's scattered troops, obtaining tens of thousands of men, and counterattacked Xiang Yu at Chengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's younger brother Tian Heng rallied the scattered soldiers of Qi, assembling tens of thousands of men, and struck back against Xiang Yu at Chengyang.

sentences.zh: 而漢王率諸侯敗楚，入彭城。

translations.literal: But the Han king led the various lords, defeated Chu, and entered Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile, the King of Han led a coalition of lords to defeat Chu and seized Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 項羽聞之，乃醳齊而歸，擊漢於彭城，因連與漢戰，相距滎陽。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu heard of it and abandoned Qi to return, striking Han at Pengcheng. He then continuously battled with Han, confronting each other at Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang Yu learned of this, he abandoned the Qi campaign and rushed south to strike the Han forces at Pengcheng. From then on, the two sides fought a protracted war, facing off at Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 以故田橫復得收齊城邑，立田榮子廣為齊王，而橫相之，專國政，政無巨細皆斷於相。

translations.literal: Therefore, Tian Heng was again able to gather Qi's cities and towns. He established Tian Rong's son Guang as King of Qi, while Heng served as his chancellor, monopolizing the state's government. All matters of government, great and small, were decided by the chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: With Xiang Yu's attention diverted, Tian Heng recovered the cities of Qi. He installed Tian Rong's son Guang as King of Qi and served as his chancellor, concentrating all power in his own hands. Every affair of state, great or small, was decided by the chancellor.

sentences.zh: 橫定齊三年，漢王使酈生往說下齊王廣及其相國橫。

translations.literal: After Heng had pacified Qi for three years, the Han king sent Li Sheng to go and persuade the submission of King Guang of Qi and his prime minister Heng.
translations.idiomatic: After Heng had held Qi for three years, the King of Han sent the persuader Li Yiji to talk King Guang of Qi and his Chancellor Heng into surrendering.

sentences.zh: 橫以為然，解其歷下軍。

translations.literal: Heng thought this was right and disbanded his army at Lixia.
translations.idiomatic: Heng found the arguments persuasive and stood down his garrison at Lixia.

sentences.zh: 漢將韓信引兵且東擊齊。

translations.literal: The Han general Han Xin led troops and was about to attack Qi to the east.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile, the Han general Han Xin was leading his army east to attack Qi.

sentences.zh: 齊初使華無傷、田解軍於歷下以距漢，漢使至，乃罷守戰備，縱酒，且遣使與漢平。

translations.literal: Qi had initially sent Hua Wushang and Tian Jie to station troops at Lixia to resist Han. When the Han envoy arrived, they stopped their guard and battle preparations, indulged in drinking wine, and moreover sent envoys to make peace with Han.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had previously stationed Hua Wushang and Tian Jie with troops at Lixia to hold off Han. But after the Han envoy arrived, they relaxed their defenses, gave themselves over to drinking, and dispatched envoys to negotiate peace with Han.

sentences.zh: 漢將韓信已平趙、燕，用蒯通計，度平原，襲破齊歷下軍，因入臨淄。

translations.literal: The Han general Han Xin had already pacified Zhao and Yan. Using Kuai Tong's plan, he crossed the Pingyuan, attacked and broke the Qi army at Lixia, and then entered Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xin, having already subdued Zhao and Yan, adopted Kuai Tong's stratagem and crossed the plains to launch a surprise attack on the Qi forces at Lixia. He then marched straight into Linzi.

sentences.zh: 齊王廣、相橫怒，以酈生賣己，而亨酈生。

translations.literal: King Guang of Qi and Chancellor Heng were angry, thinking Li Sheng had betrayed them, and cooked Li Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: King Guang and Chancellor Heng were furious, convinced that Li Yiji had sold them out. They had him boiled alive.

sentences.zh: 齊王廣東走高密，相橫走博（陽），守相田光走城陽，將軍田既軍於膠東。

translations.literal: King Guang of Qi fled east to Gaomi; Chancellor Heng fled to Boyang; the defending chancellor Tian Guang fled to Chengyang; General Tian Ji encamped his army in Jiaodong.
translations.idiomatic: King Guang fled east to Gaomi; Chancellor Heng escaped to Boyang; the Deputy Chancellor Tian Guang retreated to Chengyang; and General Tian Ji encamped with his forces in Jiaodong.

sentences.zh: 楚使龍且救齊，齊王與合軍高密。

translations.literal: Chu sent Long Ju to save Qi, and the King of Qi combined forces with him at Gaomi.
translations.idiomatic: Chu dispatched Long Ju to rescue Qi, and the King of Qi joined forces with him at Gaomi.

sentences.zh: 漢將韓信與曹參破殺龍且，虜齊王廣。

translations.literal: The Han general Han Xin, together with Cao Shen, broke and killed Long Ju, capturing King Guang of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The Han general Han Xin, together with Cao Shen, defeated and killed Long Ju and took King Guang of Qi prisoner.

sentences.zh: 漢將灌嬰追得齊守相田光。

translations.literal: The Han general Guan Ying pursued and captured Qi's defender chancellor Tian Guang.
translations.idiomatic: The Han general Guan Ying pursued and captured the Qi Deputy Chancellor Tian Guang.

sentences.zh: 至博（陽），而橫聞齊王死，自立為齊王，還擊嬰，嬰敗橫之軍於嬴下。

translations.literal: When he reached Boyang, Heng heard that the King of Qi was dead. He proclaimed himself King of Qi, turned back to attack Guan Ying, and Guan Ying defeated Heng's army below Ying.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached Boyang that the King of Qi was dead, Heng proclaimed himself King of Qi and turned to attack Guan Ying. But Guan Ying routed Heng's forces below Ying.

sentences.zh: 田橫亡走梁，歸彭越。

translations.literal: Tian Heng fled and went to Liang, joining Peng Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Heng fled to Liang and took refuge with Peng Yue.

sentences.zh: 彭越是時居梁地，中立，且為漢，且為楚。

translations.literal: Peng Yue at this time resided in Liang territory, maintaining neutrality, sometimes for Han, sometimes for Chu.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Peng Yue occupied the territory of Liang and maintained a position of neutrality, siding now with Han, now with Chu.

sentences.zh: 韓信已殺龍且，因令曹參進兵破殺田既於膠東，使灌嬰破殺齊將田吸於千乘。

translations.literal: After Han Xin had killed Long Ju, he ordered Cao Shen to advance troops and break and kill Tian Ji at Jiaodong, and had Guan Ying break and kill the Qi general Tian Xi at Qiancheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Han Xin killed Long Ju, he sent Cao Shen to advance into Jiaodong and destroy Tian Ji, and dispatched Guan Ying to defeat and kill the Qi general Tian Xi at Qiancheng.

sentences.zh: 韓信遂平齊，乞自立為齊假王，漢因而立之。

translations.literal: Han Xin then pacified Qi and begged to establish himself as acting King of Qi, and Han therefore established him as such.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xin thus completed the conquest of Qi and petitioned to be made its Acting King. The King of Han granted his request.

sentences.zh: 後歲餘，漢滅項籍，漢王立為皇帝，以彭越為梁王。

translations.literal: After more than a year, Han extinguished Xiang Ji, and the Han king established himself as emperor, making Peng Yue King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later, Han destroyed Xiang Ji. The King of Han ascended as Emperor and made Peng Yue King of Liang.

sentences.zh: 田橫懼誅，而與其徒屬五百餘人入海，居島中。

translations.literal: Tian Heng feared execution and, together with over five hundred of his followers, entered the sea and resided on an island.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Heng, fearing execution, sailed out to sea with more than five hundred of his followers and took up residence on an island.

sentences.zh: 高帝聞之，以為田橫兄弟本定齊，齊人賢者多附焉，今在海中不收，後恐為亂，乃使使赦田橫罪而召之。

translations.literal: The Gao Emperor heard of this and thought that the Tian Heng brothers had originally pacified Qi, and many worthy men of Qi were attached to them. If they were not brought in from the sea now, he feared they might cause chaos later. He then sent an envoy to pardon Tian Heng's crime and summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao heard of this and reflected that the Tian brothers had been the ones to pacify Qi, and that many of the ablest men in Qi were devoted to them. If they were left at large on the sea, they might one day stir up trouble. He therefore sent an envoy to pardon Tian Heng and summon him to court.

sentences.zh: 田橫因謝曰：「臣亨陛下之使酈生，今聞其弟酈商為漢將而賢，臣恐懼，不敢奉詔，請為庶人，守海島中。」

translations.literal: Tian Heng thereupon declined, saying, "Your servant boiled Your Majesty's envoy Li Yiji. Now I hear that his younger brother Li Shang is a Han general and a man of ability. Your servant is afraid and dares not obey the summons. I beg to remain a commoner and guard my island in the sea."
translations.idiomatic: Tian Heng declined, saying, "I boiled Your Majesty's envoy Li Yiji alive. Now I hear that his younger brother Li Shang serves as a Han general and is a man of ability. I am terrified and dare not obey the summons. I beg leave to remain a commoner and keep to my island."

sentences.zh: 使還報，高皇帝乃詔衛尉酈商曰：「齊王田橫即至，人馬從者敢動搖者致族夷！」

translations.literal: When the envoy returned and reported, Emperor Gao issued an edict to the Commandant of Guards, Li Shang, saying, "When Tian Heng, King of Qi, arrives, if any man or horse among his followers dares to stir, his clan shall be exterminated to the last!"
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy returned with this reply, Emperor Gao issued an edict to Li Shang, the Commandant of Guards: "Tian Heng, the former King of Qi, is about to arrive. If anyone among his retinue so much as stirs, the offender's entire clan shall be exterminated!"

sentences.zh: 乃復使使持節具告以詔商狀，曰：「田橫來，大者王，小者乃侯耳；

translations.literal: He then sent another envoy bearing the imperial tally to inform Tian Heng fully of the edict to Li Shang, saying, "If Tian Heng comes, at most he will be made a king, at least a marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent another envoy bearing the imperial tally to inform Tian Heng in full of the edict restraining Li Shang, adding, "If Tian Heng comes, at best he shall be made a king, at least a marquis.

sentences.zh: 不來，且舉兵加誅焉。」

translations.literal: If he does not come, troops will be raised to punish him."
translations.idiomatic: If he does not come, troops will be sent to destroy him."

sentences.zh: 田橫乃與其客二人乘傳詣雒陽。

translations.literal: Tian Heng then, together with two of his guests, rode a relay chariot to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Heng then set out with two of his retainers, traveling by relay carriage toward Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 未至三十里，至尸鄉廄置，橫謝使者曰：「人臣見天子當洗沐。」

translations.literal: Before they had gone thirty li, they reached the relay station at Shixiang. Heng declined to the envoy, saying, "When a subject is to see the Son of Heaven, he ought to bathe and purify himself."
translations.idiomatic: When they were still thirty li from the capital, they reached the relay station at Shixiang. Heng addressed the envoy, "A subject about to be received by the Son of Heaven ought first to bathe and purify himself."

sentences.zh: 止留。

translations.literal: He stopped and stayed.
translations.idiomatic: He halted there and remained.

sentences.zh: 謂其客曰：「橫始與漢王俱南面稱孤，今漢王為天子，而橫乃為亡虜而北面事之，其恥固已甚矣。

translations.literal: He said to his guests, "At first I and the King of Han both faced south and styled ourselves sovereigns; now the King of Han is Son of Heaven, while I am a fugitive captive who must face north and serve him—the shame is already very great.
translations.idiomatic: He said to his retainers, "At first I and the King of Han both faced south and styled ourselves sovereign. Now the King of Han is Son of Heaven, and I am nothing but a fugitive who must face north and serve him. The shame of it is already beyond bearing.

sentences.zh: 且吾亨人之兄，與其弟并肩而事其主，縱彼畏天子之詔，不敢動我，我獨不愧於心乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, I boiled a man's elder brother alive, and am to stand shoulder to shoulder with his younger brother in serving the same lord. Even if he fears the Son of Heaven's edict and dares not touch me, can I alone feel no shame in my heart?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, I boiled a man's elder brother alive, and now I am to stand shoulder to shoulder with his younger brother in serving the same lord. Even if Li Shang fears the imperial edict and dares not touch me, can I alone feel no shame in my heart?

sentences.zh: 且陛下所以欲見我者，不過欲一見吾面貌耳。

translations.literal: Moreover, the reason Your Majesty wishes to see me is no more than to look upon my face once.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the only reason His Majesty wishes to see me is to look upon my face once.

sentences.zh: 今陛下在洛陽，今斬吾頭，馳三十里閒，形容尚未能敗，猶可觀也。」

translations.literal: His Majesty is now in Luoyang. If my head is cut off now and rushed thirty li, my features will not yet have decayed—he may still look upon them."
translations.idiomatic: His Majesty is in Luoyang. If my head is cut off now and rushed there at a gallop—a mere thirty li—my features will not yet have decayed. He may still look upon them."

sentences.zh: 遂自剄，令客奉其頭，從使者馳奏之高帝。

translations.literal: He then slit his own throat and ordered his guest to present his head, following the envoy to gallop and present it to the Gao Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: With that he cut his own throat. He ordered his guest to present his head; the guest followed the envoy and rode at a gallop to present it to Emperor Gao.

sentences.zh: 高帝曰：「嗟乎，有以也夫！

translations.literal: Emperor Gao said, "Alas! There was reason in it!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao exclaimed, "Alas! There was something to this man indeed!

sentences.zh: 起自布衣，兄弟三人更王，豈不賢乎哉！」

translations.literal: Rising from common cloth, three brothers took the throne in turn—were they not worthy men!"
translations.idiomatic: Rising from common cloth, three brothers took the throne in turn—were they not men of surpassing worth!"

sentences.zh: 為之流涕，而拜其二客為都尉，發卒二千人，以王者禮葬田橫。

translations.literal: He shed tears for him and appointed his two guests as commandants, sending two thousand troops to bury Tian Heng with the rites of a king.
translations.idiomatic: He wept for Tian Heng, appointed the two retainers as commandants, and dispatched two thousand soldiers to bury Tian Heng with the rites due a king.

sentences.zh: 既葬，二客穿其冢旁孔，皆自剄，下從之。

translations.literal: After the burial, the two guests dug holes beside his tomb, all slit their throats, and descended to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial, the two retainers dug openings beside his tomb, slit their own throats, and fell into the earth to follow their lord in death.

sentences.zh: 高帝聞之，乃大驚，大田橫之客皆賢。

translations.literal: The Gao Emperor heard of this and was greatly astonished, praising that all of Tian Heng's guests were worthy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao heard of this, he was deeply shaken and declared that all of Tian Heng's followers were men of the highest worth.

sentences.zh: 吾聞其餘尚五百人在海中，使使召之。

translations.literal: He heard that more than five hundred of them still remained at sea and sent envoys to summon them.
translations.idiomatic: He learned that some five hundred followers still remained on the island and sent envoys to summon them.

sentences.zh: 至則聞田橫死，亦皆自殺。

translations.literal: When they arrived and heard that Tian Heng had died, they all committed suicide as well.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys arrived and the followers learned that Tian Heng was dead, every one of them took his own life.

sentences.zh: 於是乃知田橫兄弟能得士也。

translations.literal: Then he knew that the Tian Heng brothers were able to attract worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did the world understand the power the Tian brothers had to command the loyalty of men.

sentences.zh: 太史公曰：甚矣蒯通之謀，亂齊驕淮陰，其卒亡此兩人！

translations.literal: The Grand Historian says: How extreme was Kuai Tong's scheming! It threw Qi into turmoil and made the Marquis of Huaiyin arrogant—and in the end destroyed these two men!
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Historian remarks: How far-reaching was Kuai Tong's scheming! It threw Qi into turmoil and made the Marquis of Huaiyin overreach—and in the end it cost both men their lives!

sentences.zh: 蒯通者，善為長短說，論戰國之權變，為八十一首。

translations.literal: Kuai Tong was skilled at long and short speeches, discussing the power shifts of the Warring States period. He composed eighty-one chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Kuai Tong was a master of persuasive rhetoric. He composed eighty-one essays analyzing the shifting balances of power during the Warring States period.

sentences.zh: 通善齊人安期生，安期生嘗干項羽，項羽不能用其筴。

translations.literal: Tong was friendly with the Qi man An Qisheng. An Qisheng once petitioned Xiang Yu, but Xiang Yu could not use his strategies.
translations.idiomatic: Tong was on good terms with An Qisheng, a man of Qi. An Qisheng once offered his counsel to Xiang Yu, but Xiang Yu proved unable to make use of his stratagems.

sentences.zh: 已而項羽欲封此兩人，兩人終不肯受，亡去。

translations.literal: Afterward, Xiang Yu wished to enfeoff these two men, but they finally were unwilling to receive it and fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Xiang Yu wished to enfeoff both men, but they refused to accept and disappeared.

sentences.zh: 田橫之高節，賓客慕義而從橫死，豈非至賢！

translations.literal: Tian Heng's lofty integrity—guests who admired his righteousness followed him in death—were they not supremely worthy!
translations.idiomatic: As for Tian Heng's lofty integrity—that his followers so admired his sense of honor as to follow him in death—were they not men of the highest virtue!

sentences.zh: 余因而列焉。

translations.literal: I therefore list them here.
translations.idiomatic: I have therefore set down their account here.

sentences.zh: 不無善畫者，莫能圖，何哉？

translations.literal: It is not that there are no skilled painters; none has been able to depict them—why is that?
translations.idiomatic: It is not for want of skilled painters that none has been able to capture their likeness—but why should that be?
